summary: Twelve comment-endorsed home-automation tools, apps, games, hardware, and books from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 12 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: mitsubishi2MQTT
items.source_story_title: I added a non-wi-fi Mitsubishi AC to Home Assistant
items.summary: ESP8266/ESP32 firmware connecting Mitsubishi HVAC units to Home Assistant via MQTT.
items.why_included: A long-term user said it has worked great for several years.
items.evidence: The commenter reported years of successful use with Home Assistant.

evidence_sources.author: webinar
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using mitsubishi2MQTT with Home Assistant. It's been working great for several years.

items.name: ProtoART ClimateControl
items.source_story_title: I added a non-wi-fi Mitsubishi AC to Home Assistant
items.summary: A local Wi-Fi controller and sensor for Mitsubishi heat pumps and air conditioners.
items.why_included: A year-long user praised its simple setup and fully local operation.
items.evidence: The commenter was very pleased after a year and valued the straightforward local design.

evidence_sources.author: nemosaltat
evidence_sources.excerpt: A year in, I’m very pleased. Matter or thread would be nice, but these are super straightforward out of the box and totally local.

items.name: ESP32-Faikout
items.source_story_title: I added a non-wi-fi Mitsubishi AC to Home Assistant
items.summary: An open ESP32 controller giving Daikin air conditioners local Home Assistant control.
items.why_included: A Daikin owner said it works great and avoids the vendor cloud.
items.evidence: The commenter uses Faikout successfully from Home Assistant instead of Daikin's cloud service.

evidence_sources.author: damascus_kei
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Faikout(ESP32 that controls the heads via the debug port) to control my units from home assistant. Works great!

items.name: XREAL AR glasses
items.summary: Lightweight wired display glasses that create a large phone or laptop workspace.
items.why_included: A user praised their low weight and practical coding setup with Samsung DeX.
items.evidence: The commenter found the glasses unobtrusive and capable enough for office coding.

evidence_sources.author: jjmarr
evidence_sources.excerpt: Been doing this with my wired XREALs for the past few months. They are light enough to be unnoticeable and can display a large monitor when plugged into my phone or computer.

items.name: Xteink X3
items.source_story_title: How my e-reader lost its stripes
items.summary: A tiny pocket e-reader that supports community CrossPoint firmware and KOReader sync.
items.why_included: A recent buyer praised its price, pocketable form factor, and comfortable reading.
items.evidence: The commenter called the form factor amazing and said the small screen works well.

evidence_sources.author: asveikau
evidence_sources.excerpt: I got an X3 a couple of weeks ago, they are dirt cheap and the form factor is amazing. It's so easy to leave it in the pocket and just pull it out when you have an idle moment somewhere out in public.

items.name: Opair
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (September 2026)
items.summary: A coding harness with driver and read-only navigator modes for tighter pairing.
items.why_included: Its creator uses it daily and strongly endorsed the tailored pair-programming workflow.
items.evidence: The author described Opair as a perfect daily driver for staying involved in code changes.

evidence_sources.author: philbo
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use it as my daily driver and it's perfect (for me). I recommend everyone should consider writing their own harness.

items.name: Kan
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (September 2026)
items.summary: An offline Kanban board stored as plain text alongside a Git repository.
items.why_included: Its maintainer uses it across projects and finds it effective for agentic work.
items.evidence: The author praised Kan's CLI-backed workflow for helping agents track and use project state.

evidence_sources.author: amterp
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'm finding it really good for agentic work these days as, using the kan CLI, agents do really well with it for tracking work and leveraging the board. I'm using it for all my projects these days.

items.name: Flexito
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (September 2026)
items.summary: An account-free PWA with short stretching routines, custom workouts, videos, and timers.
items.why_included: Its creator uses it daily and designed five-minute routines for desk-work breaks.
items.evidence: The author reported daily use and highlighted short routines suitable for work breaks.

evidence_sources.author: nemwiz
evidence_sources.excerpt: Now I use it daily. The app is simple, you have about 100 routines to pick from and you can even build your own from existing exercises.

items.name: Three Body Orbits
items.source_story_title: An atlas of periodic solutions to the three-body problem
items.summary: An interactive atlas visualizing periodic solutions to the three-body problem.
items.why_included: A commenter strongly praised its organization, animation, and visual presentation.
items.evidence: The atlas was described as smooth, beautiful, mesmerizing, and fascinating.

evidence_sources.author: mr_mitm
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's well organized, the animations are smooth, and it looks beautiful... I'm not sure what to do with the information, but it's mesmerizing and fascinating. Great find!

items.name: Vehicles: Experiments in Synthetic Psychology
items.source_story_title: EuroBirdPortal – Live bird movements across Europe
items.summary: Valentino Braitenberg's thought experiments connecting simple machines to lifelike behavior.
items.why_included: A commenter named it as one of their favorite books.
items.evidence: The book received an unambiguous personal endorsement in a discussion of simulated flocking.

evidence_sources.author: lioeters
evidence_sources.excerpt: One of my favorite books is Vehicles: Experiments in Synthetic Psychology.

items.name: Enemy Mind
items.summary: A shooter where players possess enemy ships and consume their resources.
items.why_included: A former player called its possession mechanic fun and worth the discounted price.
items.evidence: The commenter endorsed the central ship-possession concept while noting the game is short.

evidence_sources.author: latexr
evidence_sources.excerpt: Enemy Mind is a fun tangential concept where instead of having your own ammo and life, you’re constantly possessing enemy ships and using their resources, before discarding them for the next one.

items.name: Pop!_OS
items.source_story_title: Microsoft patches Windows and Excel – breaks audio, remote access, and paste
items.summary: System76's Ubuntu-based Linux distribution with the COSMIC desktop environment.
items.why_included: A Linux daily driver said they use Pop!_OS almost everywhere and adore the desktop.
items.evidence: The commenter endorsed Pop!_OS from broad daily use across multiple device classes.

evidence_sources.author: rpdillon
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Pop!_OS almost everywhere, but Debian/Ubuntu/Arch with IceWM or Fluxbox (or the like) works great.
